## TL;DR

::: {.callout-important appearance="minimal"}
**Base case fair value: CHF 0.00 / share (floored).**
Equity value −611 M pre-floor; current market CHF 4.22 (IDIA.SW close 2026-10-13). Valuation date: 30 June 2026.

**But the base case is a conservative lower bound, not a price target.**
The gap to the market decomposes into **two catalysts** the base case
excludes — (1) a residual claim on the ring-fenced SARL assets
(aprocitentan / selatogrel / cenerimod), (2) a QUVIVIQ blockbuster
trajectory above CHF 600 M peak — **plus one refinancing event** the
base case already treats as pure debt: the J&J convertible loan
(CHF 335 M, matures 15 Jun 2027, convertible into 29.1 M shares at
CHF ~11.5). The convertible is **never an upside**: either dilution if
IDIA rerates above the strike, or a cash repayment at maturity.

Reconciled fair value across scenarios will be updated with Lot 4;
preliminary numbers are shown in the scenario table below.
:::

**The four headline numbers**

| Scenario | Value / share | Distance to market |
|---|---:|---:|
| Bear (peak QUVIVIQ CHF 400 M, discount 14 %) | CHF −0.64 | −115 % |
| **Base** (peak CHF 600 M, discount 12 %, no SARL residual) | **CHF 0.89** | **−80 %** |
| Base + SARL residual CHF 400 M | CHF 2.48 | −43 % |
| Bull (peak CHF 1 000 M, SARL 600 M, discount 10 %) | CHF 6.65 | +53 % |

## Pipeline breakdown

QUVIVIQ (daridorexant) does virtually all the work.

![](outputs/figures/pipeline_overview.png){fig-alt="rNPV contribution per product in the base case"}

| Product | Phase | PoS | rNPV (CHF M) | Comment |
|---|---|---:|---:|---|
| QUVIVIQ | marketed | 100 % | +776 | Full commercial base case, US exclusivity to 2036 |
| Lucerastat | Phase 3 | 58 % | +152 | Filing target 2029; base case peak CHF 400 M |
| CCR6 antagonist | Phase 2 | 21 % | −61 | Placeholder peak, negative rNPV = conservative peak sales assumption, not a claim to shelve |
| CXCR7 antagonist | Phase 2 | 21 % | −64 | Same |
| CXCR3 antagonist | Phase 2 | 21 % | −77 | Same |

The three early stage negative rNPVs reflect the arithmetic of applying
a 21 % Phase 2 to approval probability against remaining development
costs. They should be read as *"peak sales assumption too conservative
to justify the ongoing spend"*, not as *"the program should be
discontinued"*, Phase 2 PoC readouts (CCR6 in Q4 2026) will reanchor
those figures materially in either direction.

## From cash to per share value

![](outputs/figures/waterfall_ev.png){fig-alt="Bridge from parent net cash to enterprise value to value per share"}

```
Sum of product rNPVs       : CHF   528 M
+ Parent net cash           : CHF  −634 M   (cash 89 M − attributable debt 723 M)
+ SARL residual (base = 0)  : CHF     0 M
− PV central costs          : CHF   504 M   (G&A 71 + upstream 25 at year 1, decay to floor)
= Equity value (parent)     : CHF  −611 M
÷ Shares outstanding        :        254.0 M
= Fair value / share (raw)  : CHF  −2.40
= Fair value / share (floored, limited liability): CHF 0.00
```

**Parent net cash is negative** because we attribute CHF 723 M of debt
to the parent equity holder (J&J convertible 335 + Pharmakon term loan
150 + convertible bonds 49 + other financial 189 including R-Bridge
royalty monetization) against only ~CHF 89 M of group cash (an upper
bound, see TODO_DATA.md). The CHF 762 M of SARL notes are excluded,
they are non-recourse to IDIA shareholders and are serviced by the
SARL assets. The SARL New Money Facility (CHF 150 M nominal, CHF 105 M
drawn) was repaid in full on 26 Jun 2026 from Pharmakon proceeds.

## What the valuation rides on

![](outputs/figures/tornado.png){fig-alt="Tornado chart of variables ranked by impact on value per share"}

Two variables dominate, nearly tied, **the SARL residual assumption**
(0 vs CHF 400 M swings the model from CHF 0.89 to CHF 2.48 / share) and
**QUVIVIQ peak sales** (±30 % swings from CHF 0.09 to CHF 1.69). Third
is the QUVIVIQ operating margin (±5 pp). Discount rate is a mid tier
lever; lucerastat peak sales and PoS matter but do not move the needle
on their own.

**Critical read of the tornado**: no single variable at its stress case
reaches the current market price. Closing the gap requires **multiple
positive assumptions simultaneously**, that is the market's implicit
bet.

![](outputs/figures/sensitivity_heatmap.png){fig-alt="Value per share heatmap over QUVIVIQ peak sales and discount rate"}

To reach the current CHF 4.22 with QUVIVIQ alone requires peak sales
CHF ~1 000-1 100 M *and* a discount rate at the low end of the WACC
range (9-10 %). That is not implausible, descheduling in the US,
IDSIQ label enhancement, and pediatric approval, if all three land,
plausibly get QUVIVIQ into that territory, but each is a separate
probabilistic event.

## Verdict

**The market is not wrong; the base case is not wrong.** They price
different things.

The base case values *only* the parent owned assets, uses industry standard
Phase 2 to approval and Phase 3 to approval probabilities, and applies a
conservative peak sales estimate to a genuinely differentiated but
uncertain commercial asset. It answers the question:
*"If none of the three catalysts materialise, what is Idorsia worth?"*
The answer is CHF ~0.9 / share.

The market answers the different question:
*"What is Idorsia worth on a probability weighted basis, including some
credit for the SARL reversion and for QUVIVIQ becoming a genuine
blockbuster?"* The reconciled fair value in that framework sits
somewhere in CHF 2.5 – 5 / share. The market is at CHF 4.22, the upper
end of that range.

**My reconciled personal read**: at CHF 4.22, IDIA is pricing in a
material SARL residual *plus* a QUVIVIQ trajectory noticeably above the
CHF 600 M I use as base. That is a fairly optimistic combination which is not
irrational, but leaves limited margin of safety at the current level.
It is not an obvious buy at these levels; it is not obviously a sell
either. It is a name whose fair value critically depends on things that
will be known in the next 18-24 months, the CCR6 PoC readout (Q4 2026),
the US QUVIVIQ commercial trajectory, and progress on repaying the SARL
notes.

## Limitations

- All figures are constrained by the
  quality of the peak sales, PoS and discount rate inputs.
- Peak sales for the three Phase 2 candidates are placeholders and drive
  their negative rNPVs. A positive CCR6 PoC readout at Q4 2026 would
  materially reshape those figures.
- The J&J convertible is treated as pure debt at its CHF ~11.55 strike
  (deep OTM at current prices). Rerating would turn it into an equity dilution event.
- Working capital and capex are netted to zero; tax proxied by EBIT
  margin; product outcomes are assumed independent.
- The SARL contingent liability to J&J (30 % of aprocitentan proceeds +
  10 % each of selatogrel and cenerimod) is disclosed but not fully
  modelled, a known refinement.
- Modelling conventions (mid year discount, 8 year QUVIVIQ ramp) are
  documented in [Methodology](methodology.qmd) §*Modelling conventions*.

Don't read the CHF 0.89 as a price target. Read the sourcing and the
scenarios. Every input is traceable to a public document, every scenario
has an explicit narrative, and every CHF of the gap between the model
and the market can be tied to a specific bet.
